root_cause.text: The firmware log buffer indices (read_index and write_index) provided by the NPU firmware were not validated against the buffer size, allowing an attacker-controlled firmware to supply out-of-bounds indices and cause out-of-bounds memory access.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit checks `if (log_start >= data_size)` and `if (log_end > data_size)` to clamp the indices to safe values, and the CVE description states this prevents "potential out-of-bounds buffer access when firmware supplies invalid log indices."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds checks for log_start and log_end to prevent out-of-bounds access when printing firmware log buffer.
intent_record.what: Added two conditional assignments: if log_start is >= data_size, set it to 0; if log_end > data_size, set it to data_size.
intent_record.how: Prevents potential out-of-bounds read access when using log_start and log_end as indices into the log buffer by clamping them to valid ranges.

grouping_result.intent: Add bounds checks for log_start and log_end to prevent out-of-bounds access when printing firmware log buffer.

relevance_review.reason: The group adds bounds checks for firmware log buffer indices, directly addressing the lack of validation that caused out-of-bounds access per the root cause.

candidates.rationale: Reads the firmware-controlled read_index without validation; an attacker can supply out-of-bounds values, leading to out-of-bounds memory access when log_start is used to index the log buffer.

Reads the firmware-controlled write_index without validation; an attacker can supply out-of-bounds values, leading to out-of-bounds memory access when log_end is used as a bound or index in subsequent buffer operations.
